policy_results.detail: Classified multi-step; bug-resolution graph followed node by node. Every file was read before being edited. Unrelated work was preserved: no backend module, risk rail, or existing CI job was modified.

No secrets added or read. The audit found the backend's hardcoded demo@example.com/demo123 login branch and its unvalidated HTTPBearer dependency; both are recorded in PRIVATE_BETA_STATUS.md and deliberately NOT changed, because authentication and authorization are human-approval paths and **/*auth* is a sensitive path. The billing/checkout flow was likewise left untouched. .github/workflows/** is a sensitive path and was changed: the change adds a validation-only job, grants no permissions, and is flagged for review in the pull request.

The native client remains quarantined (app.json releaseStatus quarantined-private-web-only, eas.json has no production profile, submit-to-stores.sh still exits 64). Nothing in this change enables a build, a store submission, or a deployment.

completion_status is 'tested', not 'verified'. Every command listed was executed in this session with the recorded exit code, including the deliberately failing high-severity audit and the mutation check. No completion claim is made for anything not run here: no build, no device run, no live-backend call.

security_results.detail: 13 tests assert that with an empty or failing API each screen renders an explicit unavailable state containing none of the previously hardcoded literals. Verified non-vacuous by reintroducing '95.2% Accuracy' into the SignalsScreen header, observing 2 test failures, and reverting.

The SDK still exposes no placeOrder/cancelOrder path, TradingScreen still hands off to the user's own broker, and the misleading 'Trade Now' button that only called subscribeToSignal was removed. A test asserts the non-advice disclaimer renders and that no order-placement affordance appears.
No file matching **/*auth* was modified. The backend's missing token validation and demo credential branch are documented as open blockers requiring human approval.
ProfileScreen.handleUpgrade, the hardcoded Stripe price id, and the $29.99/month card are unchanged and recorded as an open blocker.
Diff contains no credentials. The only email literals are example.invalid test fixtures.
The workflow's top-level 'permissions: contents: read' is unchanged; the new job adds no permissions block and no secret reference.

unresolved_risks: State is 'tested', not 'verified'. No build was produced, no device or simulator ran the app, and no screen was exercised against a live backend.

The backend fabricates data too: trading_bot/api/mobile_routes.py returns price 150.25 for every symbol and fixed portfolio positions. The client now renders whatever the endpoint returns, so honest client output depends on those handlers being made real.

The client calls /portfolio, /signals/latest and /market/... while the router declares prefix /api/mobile, so every call would 404 even if the router were enabled. Deliberately not patched: fixing the path would point the app at endpoints whose bearer tokens are never validated.

9 high-severity npm advisories (postcss, image-size) remain in Expo's build toolchain. npm reports the only fix as expo@57, an SDK 54->57 major upgrade. The CI audit gate is therefore set at critical, with a separate informational step keeping the high findings visible.
expo-doctor is non-blocking in CI because it validates against Expo's remote schema and the React Native directory API; an upstream outage would otherwise redden unrelated pull requests.
The mobile test suite covers rendering only. There is no navigation, integration, or end-to-end coverage, and no test exercises the WebSocket or Auth contexts, which are mocked.

rollback.procedure: Revert the commit. No schema, migration, data, or runtime configuration is involved; the native client is quarantined and not deployed. The CI job can be removed independently by deleting the 'mobile' job from .github/workflows/ci.yml.
